text:
mira: quick follow-up from the format RFC. hit a production slip where a quant shard with a stale header was accepted and later caused NaNs in a layer. thinking: add a tiny compact header probe on open + signed manifest references for deep-verify. call it 'compact-probe + manifest' flow. any pushback?

jon: paste the node log / minimal repro?

mira: short log:
```
[2026-08-12T08:12:11Z] load_shard ckpt-r3-p2.safetensors: index ok, header=missing+legacy
[2026-08-12T08:12:11Z] WARN loader: dtype mismatch expected=float16 found=quant8
[2026-08-12T08:12:11Z] RuntimeError: GEMM produced NaN at enc_layer_21
```

sasha: bummer. UX options: (A) cheap header probe on open (fail early, small read), (B) lazy verify on first execution (cheaper until you hit the bad op). I slightly prefer A for predictable failure modes.

dmitri: Hosted/Dedicated -> default to A. Private customers should be able to opt-out or relax via config.

marie: suggestion: header should be compact and signed by the serializer so we can surface provenance without fetching large checksums. e.g. a small signed manifest blob with: serializer_id, schema, epoch, mini_sig, manifest_sig_url. quick verify on open: verify manifest signature + mini_sig. Defer full checksum fetch to background.

jon: OK. That aligns with minimal runtime cost. What fields exactly?

mira: proposal for header fields (all small): magic="RSFT", version="1", serializer="redwood/quant-x", schema=1, epoch="2026-08-10-1", mini_sig="b2:9f3a7c", manifest_sig="s3://.../ckpt-r3.manifest.sig". The manifest (signed) contains full checksums for shards and a manifest-level signature.

sasha: product/UI: Console shows a per-checkpoint integrity status: "signed-header" (green) / "legacy" (amber) / "corrupt" (red). On any live flip to "corrupt" create an incident for Dedicated/Private and post a support ticket.

ops: ops concern: rejecting on open can cause reload storms during rollouts. Need a canary toggle + sampled rollout and fallback behavior. Also add dashboards for `weights.open.fail_rate` and `weights.manifest.flip_rate`.

mira: rollout idea:
- phase 0: sample probe on 2% of opens (probe_mode=sampled). emit metrics and collect replay traces.
- phase 1: require signed-header for all new uploads; legacy uploads accepted but flagged `legacy` and enqueued for background manifest verify when accessed.
- phase 2: after 30d, tenant-level opt-in toggle to reject legacy uploads. default keep legacy allowed to avoid immediate customer impact.

dmitri: runtime behaviour details:
- on open: read first N bytes (compact header) -> verify manifest signature (fast remote signature fetch cached) -> set metadata keys `serializer` and `integrity_state` (strings).
- if integrity_state=="signed_mismatch" -> attempt fallback (float32 fallback shard or previous compatible variant) and increment `weights.signed_mismatch.attempts` metric. If fallback fails, surface error to caller and mark `weights.open.failures`.
- background verifier: fetch manifest (signed) or compute digest, update integrity_state to `deep_ok` or `deep_corrupt` and emit `weights.manifest.verify` events.

jon: API impact: keep WeightSource.open() return semantics but populate metadata map with two optional string keys: `serializer_id` and `integrity_state` values: "unknown"|"signed_ok"|"signed_mismatch"|"legacy"|"deep_ok"|"deep_corrupt". Callers that ignore metadata unaffected. Minimal surface change.

marie: we should also include `manifest_version` as a string in metadata so list/console can show provenance and allow rollbacks to manifested checkpoints.

ci-bot: noted. I'll add `serializer-manifest-roundtrip` CI job: serializer writes checkpoint + signed manifest -> loader reads header and verifies signature -> background verifier computes checksum -> end-to-end assert deep_ok on success. Hook on serializer PRs.

sasha: Console design: mockups will show a manifest panel listing shard checksums, signature timestamp, and a small "reverify now" button for ops. Badge states: green (signed_ok or deep_ok), amber (legacy), red (deep_corrupt).

ops: telemetry: add dashboards for `weights.open.latency` with/without probe, `weights.signed_mismatch.rate`, `weights.manifest.verify.latency`, and set canary alerts. Also require a rollback playbook for any spike in `weights.open.failures`.

dmitri: tests: unit to parse header-only, unit to simulate signature mismatch and ensure fallback, integration that replays old-serializer headers and ensures legacy path is accepted and queued.

jon: implementation note: cache manifest signatures locally (TTL) and keep signature verification asynchronous where possible to avoid blocking cold open in heavily loaded nodes. But still fail fast on clear header signature mismatch (signed_mismatch).

mira: ops-safety: default behavior summarized: new uploads must have signed manifest; legacy uploads accepted and marked legacy; header probe enforced for Hosted/Dedicated by default; config flag per-tenant for private that controls `require_signed_manifest`.

marie: +1 for manifest+signed header approach. Gives provenance and a recovery path for corrupted shards.

ops: SGTM but please coordinate canary windows with infra calendar and include a kill-switch toggle.

mira: thanks. I'll draft a short RFC patch with header schema, signed-manifest format, WeightSource metadata keys, runtime fallback + metrics, verifier daemon, CI job, and rollout playbook. Owners: mira (author), jon (loader), marie (manifest design), sasha (console), ops (rollout). Filing now and tagging @team-eng-ml :eyes:
